title: Biodiversity metric for LUSH 3.0 developments
asked: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked whether the Government has considered complementing LUSH 3.0's focus on greenery provision with a biodiversity metric that measures net ecological gain or loss, similar to the UK's Biodiversity Net Gain framework, so that developments are assessed by measurable biodiversity improvement rather than how green they appear.
response: Mr Alvin Tan said LUSH requires developers to provide replacement greenery within new developments, up to 40% of the development site area in some cases, and that since 2009 it has supported over 440 hectares of greenery. He said the ministry assesses that Singapore's balanced and coordinated approach to enhancing biodiversity can achieve better outcomes than the UK's Biodiversity Net Gain framework, which imposes biodiversity targets on individual development projects. He cited safeguarding 7,800 hectares of green spaces, additional nature parks, habitat restoration and species recovery, and the Chencharu, Yishun project where HDB worked with biodiversity experts and nature groups on an environmental impact assessment and an environmental monitoring management plan.
